text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Yiannakis Matsis, the outgoing chairman of right-wing Disy party, launches a broadside against President Glafcos Clerides, who is the founder of Disy, for undermining the leadership and role of the party.
- Cabinet reshuffle likely to be announced today.
- Matsis stands by his decision to resign from the party leadership. "I cannot accept Disy being a secondary decision-making centre," he says.
- The government spokesman plays down rumours of a cabinet reshuffle.
- Communist Akel and Socialist Edek parties reaffirm their will to cooperate for the presidential elections in early 1998.
- the ministers of labour and interior assure unions a moratorium will be imposed in the number of foreign workers employed in industry and tourism.
- The countdown to elections begins in Disy. Party analysts see a tough election battle for the leadership between general secretary Demetris Syllouris and vice-chairman Nicos Anastassiades.
- Turkish fighter jets violated Cyprus's flight information region on Sunday.
